title: The effect of H1N1 vaccination on serum miRNA expression in children: A tale of caution for microRNA microarray studies.
ehr_evidence: Serum samples were obtained from children aged 6 months to 12 years enrolled in an open label randomised control trial of two pandemic influenza (H1N1) vaccines, in which participants received either ASO3B adjuvanted split virion or a whole virion non-adjuvanted vaccine.
summary: A randomized controlled trial sub-study profiling serum microRNA expression in children before and 21 days after H1N1 vaccination using microarray and RT-qPCR, highlighting validation challenges.
key_findings: Microarray analysis identified 19 differentially expressed miRNAs post-vaccination (fold-change >1.2, adjusted p<0.05).
RT-qPCR confirmed significant downregulation of miR-142-3p in the discovery cohort (mean log2 fold-change = -0.312, p = 0.003).
Downregulation of miR-142-3p was not replicated in the validation cohort (mean log2 fold-change = 0.15, p = 0.89).
Only 3 out of 19 differentially expressed miRNAs were detectable by RT-qPCR, with many showing no amplification or high background.
study_design: randomized controlled trial sub-study with microarray and RT-qPCR validation
limitations: lack of replication in independent validation cohort
potential false positives from microarray cross-hybridization
